rationale: Executive Order 11125 (October 29, 1963; 28 FR 11609) delegated the President's authority under sections 205 and 208(b) of title 18, United States Code, to heads of departments and agencies for certain presidential appointees. Section 703(b) of Executive Order 11222 (May 8, 1965; 30 FR 6469, held official Federal Register text) states: "The following are hereby revoked :" and lists "(b) Executive Order No. 11125 of October 29,1963." The section adds that the effective date of the revocation is the date the Civil Service Commission issues regulations under Section 701(a) of that order. The revocation names the whole order without limitation, so no part survives. The condition was met long before 2026: the held Federal Register notice FR Doc. 05-15927 states that the confidential financial disclosure regulation implementing Executive Order 11222, 5 CFR part 735 subpart D, became effective on October 1, 1965 (30 FR 12529), and Section 701(a) authorizes regulations implementing Parts II, III and IV of that order. Executive Order 11222 was itself revoked in 1989 by Executive Order 12674 (held notice FR Doc. 05-6383), but no held text revives Executive Order 11125 and a revocation of the revoking order does not by itself restore a revoked order. The exact date of the Commission's first regulations under Section 701(a) is not held, which leaves the lifecycle first-end date open but does not change the status: the order was not in force on 2026-10-14.
